text:
julia_ml: heads up — dashboard diff shows q4_0-v2 as ~3.5% better on "accuracy" vs baseline, but the sample-level drilldown for the slices where improvement is supposed to happen returns empty results :confused:
sam_dev: wait, empty drilldown? the diff panel had plenty of hits in the heatmap last night :eyes:
noah_r: I saw something similar earlier — export CSV had rows but the UI's sample modal was blank for some buckets. could be a pagination / limit UI bug or filter mismatch.
eva_eval: also saw CI eval job print a warning about seed collisions during runner replays. that could affect deterministic sample ids used by the drilldown. cc @rcarter for recent runner changes.
rcarter: re: runner — I pushed a change that switched to RFC3339 window keys for aggregation (start/end) rather than epoch buckets. UI still expects epoch-start indexes for drilldown queries. probable mismatch.
julia_ml: ahhh that'd do it. the diff view was aggregating with new window keys so counts looked right, but sample lookup used the old id path. can we reproduce?
sam_dev: I tried a local repro. run:```bash
./eval-runner --model q4_0-v2 --suite reg-1000 --out-format parquet --seed 42
``` then from the console try the drilldown query endpoint: `/api/v1/evals/samples?bucket_start=1700000000&bucket_end=1700003600&metric=accuracy` returns 0 while `/api/v1/evals/agg?metric=accuracy&window=2024-04-??` returns 27.
eva_eval: attaching the CI job that flagged the mismatch: ci-bot: build 4823 failed: eval-runner e2e (run:4823) — https://ci.internal/4823 — logs show: `WARN runner: aggregation key format changed without migration`
rcarter: patch incoming. quick plan: 1) revert runner to epoch-bucket behavior for the next patch release (safe), 2) add compatibility layer that accepts both epoch and rfc3339 window keys for UI drilldowns, 3) add a regression test in CI that runs a tiny eval and ensures drilldown sample count equals aggregated count for each window.
julia_ml: sounds good. note for QA: also check quantized variants — quantization experiments produce slightly different timing and sometimes change assignment to buckets (off-by-one ms). make sure windowing uses inclusive/exclusive bounds consistently.
sam_dev: agreed. I can add an integration test that runs q4_0-v2 vs baseline and asserts sample exports are non-empty for any non-zero aggregated buckets.
eva_eval: small improvement suggestion: return a small preview row in the UI when drilldown is empty with a hint: "No samples found for this window. Possible causes: runner window key mismatch, seed drift, or pagination." saves time.
rcarter: will add the hint. also bumping the feature flag so we can toggle compatibility layer while we monitor.
ci-bot: @rcarter created MR #8791 to add backward-compat window support and CI regression tests — https://git.internal/mr/8791 :thumbsup:
julia_ml: thanks all — moving to a follow-up thread for rollout notes once MR lands. closing loop here. :white_check_mark:
